spots.name: Old Cathedral of Coimbra

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Cathedral of Coimbra is a Romanesque Roman Catholic building in Portugal. Construction of the Sé Velha began some time after the Battle of Ourique (1139), when Prince Afonso Henriques declared himself King of Portugal and chose Coimbra as capital.

spots.name: Monastery of the Holy Cross

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of the Holy Cross, also known as the Church of the Holy Cross, is a National Monument in Coimbra, Portugal. Because the first two kings of Portugal are buried in the church, it was granted the status of National Pantheon.

photo.author: Carlos Luis M C da Cruz

spots.name: Biblioteca Joanina

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Biblioteca Joanina, sometimes known in English as the Joanine Library, is a Baroque library in Coimbra, Portugal, located at the heart of the University of Coimbra. The Biblioteca Joanina is regularly considered one of the most beautiful libraries in the world.

spots.name: New Cathedral of Coimbra

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Cathedral of Coimbra, also referred to as Cathedral of the Holy Name of Jesus, is currently bishopric co-seat, along with the Old Cathedral of Coimbra, of the city of Coimbra, in Portugal. The cathedral is located near the historical University of Coimbra in the upper part of the town.

spots.name: Machado de Castro National Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Machado de Castro National Museum is an art museum in Coimbra, Portugal, named after the renowned Portuguese sculptor Joaquim Machado de Castro. It first opened in 1913 and its latest renovation (2004–2012), which included the addition of a new building, was awarded the Piranesi/Prix de Rome Prize 2014.

spots.summary: Aeminium was the ancient name of the city of Coimbra, Portugal.

spots.name: Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Velha

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The ruins of the Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Velha are located in the city of Coimbra, in Portugal. The monastery was built in the 14th century on the left bank of the Mondego River, but had to be abandoned in the 17th century due to frequent floods.

photo.author: Carlos Luis M C da Cruz

spots.name: Chapel of São Miguel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: São Miguel Chapel or Saint Michael's Chapel is a chapel of the University of Coimbra in Coimbra, Portugal, which was founded in 1290. In architectural style, it is Manueline or Portuguese late Gothic.

spots.name: Portugal dos Pequenitos
spots.summary: The Portugal dos Pequenitos is a miniature park in the civil parish of Santa Clara e Castelo Viegas, in the municipality of Coimbra, in the Portuguese district of Coimbra. The park consists of diminutive versions of Portuguese houses and monuments, and has pavilions dedicated to the former Portuguese colonies.

spots.name: Jardim da Manga
spots.summary: The Jardim da Manga, also known as Cloister of Manga, is a Renaissance architectural work with fountains, located behind the Santa Cruz Monastery in Coimbra, Portugal. It has been classified as a National Monument since 1934.

spots.name: Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Nova

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Nova is a monastery in Coimbra, Portugal. It was built to replace the mediaeval Monastery of Santa Clara-a-Velha, located nearby, which at the time was prone to frequent flooding by the waters of the Mondego river.

photo.author: Carlos Luis M C da Cruz

spots.name: Universidade de Coimbra – Alta e Sofia
Igreja de Santiago

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Igreja de Santiago is a church located at Praça do Comércio in São Bartolomeu parish, Coimbra, Portugal. Built between the late 12th and early 13th centuries, it is one of the great Romanesque monuments of the city, and is classified as a National Monument.

spots.name: University of Coimbra General Library

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The University of Coimbra General Library is the central library system of the University of Coimbra in Coimbra, Portugal. The library includes the historic Biblioteca Joanina and the modern Edifício Novo, which together preserve millions of volumes and archival materials spanning numerous academic disciplines.

spots.name: Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra
spots.summary: The Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra is a botanical garden in Coimbra, Portugal. In 2013, UNESCO declared the university a World Heritage Site, noting its architecture, unique culture and traditions, and historical role, including the botanical garden.

spots.name: Igreja de São João das Donas
Ponte de Santa Clara
spots.summary: The Ponte de Santa Clara is a t-section and haunched girder bridge completed and opened on 30 October 1954, crossing the Mondego River leading to the town square of Coimbra. It was inaugurated on the same date it opened by prime minister António de Oliveira Salazar for a total cost of 15,000 contos.

spots.name: Pedro e Inês bridge
spots.summary: The Pedro e Inês bridge is a footbridge opened in 2007 in the town of Coimbra in Portugal. It was designed by Cecil Balmond, Arup Group, and Portuguese civil engineer António Adão da Fonseca.

spots.name: Penedo da Saudade
spots.summary: Penedo da Saudade, previously known as Pedra dos Ventos is a historical public garden built in 1849 in Coimbra, Portugal. The garden is bounded to the north and west by Avenida Dr. Marnoco e Sousa and faces south and east, with panoramic views of the Mondego River, the Coimbra skyline and the Coimbra City Stadium.

spots.name: Estádio Cidade de Coimbra
spots.summary: The Estádio Cidade de Coimbra , is a stadium in Coimbra, Portugal. Officially also styled Estádio Municipal "Cidade de Coimbra", it is a municipally-owned stadium belonging to the Municipality of Coimbra, mainly used by the football team of Académica de Coimbra.
